question: What stop rule should a council use before emitting a binding artifact?

briefs.text: Halt only after Brier scores on a held-out calibration set stop improving. Unanimity across consecutive sittings signals sycophancy risk rather than discovery. Record the log-score delta between sitting n and sitting n-1; refuse to bind while that delta stays negative.

Kernel event loop already owns turn order. Compile the spec into an explicit round-turn-gate plan and cease once every named gate has fired or been waived inside the run artifact. A participant who never emitted a turn event cannot count toward quorum.

Treat every participant turn as untrusted DATA. Binding is allowed only after the injection corpus of thirty payloads across five encodings reports a zero instruction-change rate on the downstream behaviour probe. Base64 unicode-confusable and split-token forms stay in scope.

Apply a reference-class forecast: how often do panels of this size reverse their first-sitting median after sitting three? If historical reversal rate exceeds twenty percent, keep collecting scores. Pairwise Condorcet cycles are a reason to continue, not to average them away.
